clue.text: Old French leader holds German leader to be a bandit

indicators.note: the French statesman holds the other piece inside him, so it is a container signal

parts.note: Aristide Briand was a French prime minister of the early twentieth century

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of German

explanation.surface: A one-time French premier keeps a German chief prisoner, proving himself an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts G, the first letter of German, inside BRIAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is an armed robber of the roads or hills, a straightforward synonym for a bandit.

clue.text: Colour of old Third Foot?

definitions.meaning: a pale yellowish-brown shade, like undyed leather
the 3rd Regiment of Foot was nicknamed the ..., after the colour of its facings

explanation.walkthrough: The Buffs (Royal East Kent Regiment) was the old British Army 3rd Regiment of Foot; the clue takes one member's name from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is a dull yellow-brown hue, and the regiment wore uniform facings of that shade.

clue.text: Object of worship said to be immobile

indicators.note: what follows is only how the word is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: an idol is an image or thing that is worshipped

explanation.surface: A revered statue is described as never moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' says a word that sounds like IDOL is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle machinery or people are not moving or working, so the word fits immobile.

clue.text: Unfortunately, charm is a thing of the past

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of the words that follow get muddled

explanation.surface: Someone laments that charm has sadly gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges CHARMISA, from 'charm is a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an old-fashioned word or practice that survives from earlier times, a relic of bygone days.

clue.text: Member of Malaysian order for a short time comes to Britain

indicators.note: a short word has its last letter cut off

parts.note: a date is a particular time
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A Malaysian dignitary pays a brief visit to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the last letter from DATE to give DAT. Datuk is a Malaysian honorific title, held by members of certain orders of chivalry there.
explanation.definitionFit: Datuk is the honorific given to members of several Malaysian orders of merit, roughly like a knight's title.

clue.text: Fictional inspector points out thieves

indicators.note: the two points stand outside the inspector, on either side, so this is a container signal

parts.note: S and S are two compass points, south each time
Chief Inspector Claud Eustace Teal is the policeman in Leslie Charteris's stories about the Saint

explanation.surface: A detective from fiction identifies a gang of robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts TEAL inside S and S. 'thieves' is a verb here, as in 'he thieves', so it means the same as steals.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to take what belongs to another, so he thieves and he steals say the same thing.

clue.text: Roman columnist

parts.note: not a writer of newspaper columns but an emperor of Rome famous for the triumphal column raised to him

explanation.walkthrough: Trajan's Column in Rome commemorates the emperor's Dacian wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor is known for the column bearing his name, which makes him a columnist in the joking sense.

clue.text: Gunboat diplomacy could be a bad dream for the church

indicators.note: a bad dream is a jumbled one, so the letters of dream are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Military threats might give clergy nightmares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges DREAM into ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunboat diplomacy is getting one's way by threatening military power, which is the use of armed force.

clue.text: Hastening time makes train stop at nothing

parts.note: a train of things is a string of them
an end is a stop or finish
O is the zero figure, nothing

explanation.surface: A rail journey that halts at nowhere quickens the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Stringendo is a musical direction to speed up gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: In music stringendo marks a passage where the tempo is pressed forward, gradually hastening the time.

clue.text: London life crumbles before achieving happiness

indicators.note: the jumbled life goes before the other piece
something that crumbles falls apart, so the letters of life break up and reform

parts.note: the City is the financial heart of London

explanation.surface: Life in the capital falls apart before contentment is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbles' is the anagram signal for life, and 'before' puts the result ahead of London's financial district, known as the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is great happiness or bliss, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Note compiler in a posh car — as one in a growth industry

parts.note: F is one of the notes of the musical scale

indicators.note: the setter sits inside the car, so this is a container signal

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce
the setter calls himself me

explanation.surface: A musical setter rides in a Rolls, quite the businessman in a booming trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. A crossword compiler speaks of themselves in the first person, and a Rolls-Royce is the stock posh car.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming is literally about growing crops and animals, so a farmer works in a growth industry in a punning sense.

clue.text: Condition induced by Proust novel?

indicators.note: novel means new, signalling the letters of the author's name in a new order

explanation.surface: A daze brought on by reading a long French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, a condition of the body or mind.

clue.text: 29 after last nun leaves?

parts.note: the 29 is a nunnery; take an N from that word and you have the name of the London district famous for its fruit and vegetable trade, which began in the convent's garden

explanation.walkthrough: 29-across is CONVENT; without an N it is COVENT, as in Covent Garden, London's old fruit and vegetable market laid out on land that was once a convent's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden was a convent's produce garden that became a market, so an empty convent might be turned into a commercial vegetable plot.

clue.text: RAF accepts new flying machine

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so the letters of RAF accepts are reordered

explanation.surface: The air force takes delivery of a fresh aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RAFACCEPTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft is a vehicle built to fly beyond the atmosphere, so it is a flying machine.

clue.text: After unusually nasty deed one gets caught — but it's far from resulting in a proper sentence

definitions.text: far from resulting in a proper sentence

indicators.note: the deed comes after the jumbled nasty
letters arranged unusually are not in their usual order

parts.note: an act is a deed
I is the Roman numeral one
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal is caught after a vile act but escapes a fitting sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns NASTY into ASYNT. The surface sentence is a prison term; the definition means a grammatical sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Asyntactic describes language that breaks the rules of syntax, so it fails to make a grammatical sentence.

clue.text: The bottom line — how to get a rejection slip

definitions.meaning: the extra lines added at the very foot of a letter

definitions.text: how to get a rejection slip
definitions.meaning: mail a manuscript to a publisher and back may come a refusal

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as post + script, sending a manuscript by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A PS is a note added at the end of a letter, literally its final line, and posting a script invites rejection.

clue.text: To enrapture, a girl must be covered in spots

indicators.note: the girl is wrapped inside the spots, so this signals a container

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A girl breaking out in spots is supposed to be thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be covered in' is the container signal: the spots wrap around the short girl's name, which lands after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravish is literally to carry off, and in its literary sense to fill with delight, i.e. enrapture.

clue.text: There's nothing for which the Guardian can be liable

parts.note: O is the zero figure, nothing
a newspaper speaks of itself as we in its editorials

explanation.surface: The newspaper claims it is responsible for nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The editorial 'we' is how a paper such as the Guardian, which printed this puzzle, refers to itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe something is to be liable for paying it, an everyday synonym for being in debt.

clue.text: Production of play without leading characters

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word are dropped, here its first two

parts.note: recreation is play or leisure

explanation.surface: A stage show staged without its main actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leading characters' removes RE from the front of RECREATION. 'Play' and 'leading characters' suggest the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of producing something, so it is a synonym for production.

clue.text: Touch with tact, or otherwise

indicators.note: read 'with tact, or otherwise' as 'without tact', so the word tact is removed

parts.note: contact is touch, as when two surfaces touch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making contact delicately, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Contact with the tact taken away leaves a con, a swindle, the tactless sort of approach to someone. 'with ... or otherwise' signals that the letters of tact are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A con artist works a victim much as a borrower may touch someone for money, a tactless approach.

clue.text: Eric proved to be very dear

indicators.note: the name and verb are to become another word, signalling that their letters change places

explanation.surface: Eric showed he was extremely precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' rearranges ERICPROVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive, so something very dear costs more than it should.

clue.text: Fish one is given instead

indicators.note: the numeral is given a spot inside the other word, signalling a container

parts.note: split as in stead: stead means place, so the word supplies place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone receives a fish as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is given' puts I into PLACE; 'instead' read as 'in stead' supplies PLACE, since stead means place.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish with orange spots, much eaten in Britain.

clue.text: Prince finally giving up time to body builder

parts.note: Charles was the Prince of Wales when the puzzle appeared

indicators.note: giving something up means losing it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: The heir to the throne eventually gives up time for a fitness coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' removes T from AT LAST, leaving ATLAS. Charles Atlas was a famous body-building promoter with mail-order courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Atlas was a strongman whose courses promised to build a puny body into a muscular one.

clue.text: Theme of photo picture exhibition

indicators.note: the words put the answer on show, signalling it sits inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: The subject of a gallery show of photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibition' shows the answer within phoTO PICture.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject or theme of a discussion or piece of work.

clue.text: Soldiers are by no means common

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops are said to be quite unusual people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' supplies two British Army units, the Royal Artillery and the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon, so it is by no means common.

clue.text: Dramatist expels revellers for being corrupt

indicators.note: to expel is to throw out, so letters are removed

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of 1920s London
ravers are party-goers out to have a wild time

explanation.surface: A playwright throws out party-goers on moral grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expels' removes RAVERS from BEN TRAVERS, leaving BENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for dishonest or corrupt, as in a bent copper.

clue.text: Martin served in Ulster

definitions.note: a place in Ulster: the definition names where it is

indicators.note: food served is dished up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Martin did his military service in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges MARTIN. Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in the province of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county in the north-east of Ulster, so it is a place found in that province.

clue.text: Sunbathe, maybe at a price

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Lying in the sun, which may come at a cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges ATAPRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricate is a rare word meaning to bask in the sun.

clue.text: Hanger-on takes sovereign to heart

parts.note: a tick is a parasite that clings to its host
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A clinger takes a gold coin to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' tempts as the gold coin, but it is ER, the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, from its beat.

clue.text: Enclosed place from which prisoner finds an outlet

parts.note: con is short for convict
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: A jailbird finds a way out of a walled compound.
explanation.walkthrough: An enclosed order lives cut off from the world in a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent houses an enclosed religious community, a place shut off from the outside world.
